pk_lead: The AI providers of the semantic gate, the connections to a gateway and the API keys. They are your own settings, outside every project: they apply to every project on this machine, and the screen never shows the value of a stored key.
pk_locked_governed: Governed mode: the policy {policy} fixes the configuration, and keys and preferences are not changed here. Testar is still available.
pk_locked_policy: This interface edits the CI policy: the user's keys and preferences are not changed here. Open jgates ui on a project to save them.
pk_where_keys: The keys live in the user's key store, {path} (folder 0700, file 0600). A 0600 file is not the operating system keychain: anyone using your session can read it.
pk_where_prefs: The provider preferences live in {path}, next to the key store. None of this goes to the project.
pk_where_order: The environment variable wins over the key store. In a project, jgates.yml wins over your preferences, which win over the provider's default. jgates ci uses only the environment and the policy.
pk_problems: Entries of the preferences file that were left out
pk_http_lead: Each provider uses its base URL (replaceable by a proxy), a default model and a key by the name of its variable.
pk_connections_lead: A gateway compatible with the OpenAI API (LiteLLM, vLLM, a team proxy, Ollama under /v1), with a name. A project uses the connection with provider: <name>.
pk_cli_lead: They use the CLI's own login and need no key; only the default model is kept here.
pk_other_lead: Names no provider of the list uses: your own (for example, the passEnv of a PII tool). Only the process that declares the name gets the value.
pk_docs: More about the key store and the keys: {en} ({pt} in Portuguese).
pk_help_baseUrl: http or https; http only for loopback unless you confirm it. Empty goes back to the provider's default.
pk_help_model: The model the provider uses when the project sets none. Empty leaves no default.
pk_help_apiKeyEnv: The name of the variable (or of the store entry) that holds the key, never the key. Empty goes back to the default name.
pk_help_headers: One per line, as Name: value. No credentials: Authorization, *-key and *-token are refused, the key goes in the key store.
pk_allow_http: I accept plain http without TLS for this host: the key travels in clear text over the network.
pk_test_model_missing: The default model is not in the provider's list.
pk_test_no_tokens: Only the model list was requested: no prompt sent, no token spent.
pk_models_available: {count} models of the provider to choose from.
pk_remove_connection_lead: Projects with provider: {name} no longer find the connection. The key {key} stays in the key store.
pk_reset_lead: Your preferences for {name} (base URL, model, key name) are removed and the provider's defaults apply again. The key stays in the key store.
pk_add_lead: The gateway runs on its own; the semantic gate only talks to it through the OpenAI API.
pk_add_name_help: Lowercase letters, digits and "-"; it cannot be the name of a provider.
pk_add_name_invalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and "-", starting with a letter or a digit (up to 63).
pk_add_name_reserved: This name is a provider of the semantic gate; choose another one.
pk_add_key_help: Without a name, the connection uses {name}. Save the gateway's key after the connection is created.
pk_key_env_wins: The environment variable {env} is set and takes precedence: it is the one used while it exists.
pk_key_env_wins_stored: The key store also has a value, but the environment variable {env} takes precedence: the stored value only applies when it is not set.
pk_key_hint: The value goes straight to the key store and the field is cleared; the screen never shows it back.
pk_key_hint_env: Saving in the key store changes nothing while the variable {env} is set in the environment.
pk_key_save_aria: Save key {name} in the key store
pk_key_saved: Key {name} saved in the key store.
pk_key_saved_env_wins: Key {name} saved in the key store, but the environment variable {env} still wins.
pk_key_remove_lead: The value of {name} leaves the key store. Whoever uses the key then depends on the environment variable.
pk_key_removed: Key {name} removed from the key store.
pk_key_removed_env: Key {name} removed from the key store; the environment variable {env} is still set.
pk_addkey_name_help: Capital letters, digits and "_", like the name of an environment variable.
pk_addkey_name_invalid: Use capital letters, digits and "_", not starting with a digit.
pk_addkey_name_exists: This name is already listed: use Change key on it.
